title: 2006 HMMT February Guts Problem 2
statement: Compute the positive integer less than 1000 which has exactly 29 positive proper divisors. (Here we refer to positive integer divisors other than the number itself.)

solutions.text: Recall that the number \(N=p_{1}^{e_{1}} p_{2}^{e_{2}} \cdots p_{k}^{e_{k}}\) (where the \(p_{i}\) are distinct primes) has exactly \(\left(e_{1}+1\right)\left(e_{2}+1\right) \cdots\left(e_{k}+1\right)\) positive integer divisors including itself. We seek \(N<1000\) such that this expression is 30 . Since \(30=2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5\), we take \(e_{1}=1, e_{2}=2, e_{3}=4\). Then we see that \(N=5^{1} 3^{2} 4^{2}=720\) is satisfactory.
